kata.name: Flyweight sharing law F-Intern: a format-1.3 declarative key on the intrinsic tuple catches the duplicated instance (one executed key violation; the conventional interning test catches it too — parity)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md (Flyweight row, re-opened by naming the law first); fixtures/katas/flyweight/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.8
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the candidate sharing law is expressible as injectivity of intrinsic over the declared flyweight rows; the key is expected to emit one executed violation for the colliding pair, and the conventional interning assertion is expected to name the same element, so unique is empty (parity)

expected.detail: the factory created a second instance (row 1) for the intrinsic state row 0 already holds; every client handle agrees with its key, so equation 0 is silent, and the declarative key on intrinsic fires one executed violation naming the colliding pair [0,1]. The conventional arm names the same pair element

commands: python3 prototype/flyweight_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: 2 clean + 4 fault fixtures match the pre-registered detections
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/flyweight/flyweight-fault-duplicate-intrinsic.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py --assert, executed before the probe arm: the interning-pairs assertion groups the declared rows by intrinsic tuple and names the colliding pair, the same element the key witness maps to

baseline.artifact: prototype/flyweight_baseline.py sha256:c5c9c28bc4e1bb75a7b2fb64bf41a66d908cd3fee468f7fd00150c26cdbd6d30 (scripted conventional Flyweight test: handle identity, interning pairs, pool closure)

expressibility_gap.invariant: declared instance counts and share counts (F-Capacity)
expressibility_gap.why: the key states injectivity over declared rows and reports colliding pairs; no predicate carries a numeral over instance counts (pool size, share count), so 'one shared instance per intrinsic state' is expressible only as pair existence, never as arithmetic

expressibility_gap.invariant: every declared instance is the factory's image (F-Closure)
expressibility_gap.why: injectivity is silent on a distinct-intrinsic row that no key can produce; the kernel has no surjectivity/closure predicate and `query` returns data, never a finding (recorded in the orphan entry)

discrepancies: this entry answers the expressibility question positively (the named law is executed and emits a finding) while its P6 verdict is killed: the conventional test catches the same fault, so the unique set is empty. Expressibility and advantage are separate claims; neither is inflated here.

the weak-lens-set Flyweight entry recorded zero findings on a format-1.0 fixture with no equation and no key. Its null measured that fixture, not the pattern: with the sharing law declared, the kernel emits findings for the same fault class.
procedure: 1. The law was named before the fixtures (README 'Law named first'): F-Intern (declarative key on the intrinsic tuple), F-Handle (path equation key x factory = flyweight), plus the two laws named as unexpressible (F-Closure, F-Capacity). The fault set and its expectations were pinned in fixtures/katas/flyweight/faults.json.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/flyweight_baseline.py, sha256 pinned in comparison.baseline) was executed first: the complete conventional Flyweight contract (handle identity per client, interning pairs over declared rows, pool closure), never calling catherine.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, findings recorded verbatim; no kernel change and no new CLI.

4. Witnesses were mapped to the pre-registered element vocabulary: an equation witness {equation, row} to flyweight:handle-identity@Client#<row>; a key witness {key, rows:[lo,hi]} to flyweight:interning-pair@Flyweight#<lo>/Flyweight#<hi>; baseline-only pool-closure elements carry no probe counterpart. unique = probe elements minus baseline elements.

5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived. Expressibility is recorded separately in expressibility_gap and never inflates the verdict.
